description: The bar chart, titled “Factual Errors,” illustrates the number of factual errors across three question-answering (QA) methods — NoR QA (orange with grid pattern), OneR QA (red with polka dots), and a third method represented by blue bars with diagonal stripes — evaluated on four datasets: 2WikiMQA, MuSiQue, and IIRC (with the first dataset partially obscured but identifiable by context). The vertical y-axis is scaled from 0 to 30 in increments of 5, representing the count of factual errors. For 2WikiMQA, NoR QA has 29 errors, OneR QA has 23, and the third method has 14. For MuSiQue, NoR QA has 28, OneR QA has 27, and the third method has 23. For IIRC, NoR QA has 15, OneR QA has 14, and the third method has 11. The bars are grouped by dataset along the horizontal axis, with each group containing three bars corresponding to the QA methods. The chart visually suggests that the third method (blue) consistently yields the fewest factual errors across all datasets, while NoR QA generally has the highest, except on MuSiQue where OneR QA is slightly higher. The chart is tilted diagonally in the image, and the legend is positioned in the upper right corner.
